scope: Cut257 negative-suite priority item 4 (boundary clocks, per-cast identity and conservation). Observations made while writing the controlled tests; not a claim about earned play, balance or fun.

observations.happened: The Execution 39/40 boundary test could not bash at T+39: the hero stood at (2,3) instead of (4,5) and had lost 3 hp.
observations.cause: A killed Bloat mother leaves a hazard the hero steps out of on his own rules (`choose_and_act`'s `hazard -> step out`), so by T+39 the boundary boss spawned at the kill tile was three tiles away and the melee bash was refused (`verb_attack` returns false for a bash out of reach).
observations.action: The boundary bash and kill now spawn the fresh boss adjacent to the hero's actual position, so the real melee charge and kill are asserted at both 39 and 40.
observations.confidence: high; reproduced from the observed monster/hero positions and the engine's own hazard override

observations.happened: A full-save comparison in the retained-Vanish test differed only in `game.events`.
observations.cause: `Game::save()` serializes the run's event buffer, and the buffer had been cleared after the reference save was taken.
observations.action: The reference save is captured after the event clear, as the pre-existing refusal tests do; the refusal itself emits nothing.

observations.happened: A fractional pace does not advance a ten-tick crossing (a nine-tick window cannot reach 100 from fractional bonuses alone), so 'the pace moves the next action turn' was the wrong oracle.
observations.cause: Fractional pace adds at most one energy per tick; the deficit the settlement fills is the quantity that really depends on it.
observations.action: The test pins the applied settlement energy per clock (plain 10, pace 5 six, pace 9 two) plus the exact one-tick advance against the node-free fork, and the timed speed's earlier arrival (20 vs 22).

observations.happened: In the Smoke-walk conservation pair the enabled fork ended the comparison turn with 40 energy and no extra action, while the node-free fork had 90 energy after an extra Hold.
observations.cause: The refund is applied in the completion tick before that tick's energy accrual, so it changes when the actor's own clock crosses 100.
observations.action: The conservation assertion is 'the enabled fork never acts before the cleared fork' (real energy, no node-invented action) plus world equality; the observed counts are printed.

observations.happened: No reachable real action queues a node refund with a real net debit of exactly 0.
observations.cause: `class_advanced::after_action`'s `debit` is `ACT_ENERGY - (energy after the traits' own step)`. The only 100 % energy return is `light hands` and it is gated to a taking `pick_up`, which never queues an energy refund; `sure` caps at 75 % (`retreat`/`back_corridor`/`kite`/homeward return/bank/explore) and the physical reload always records a real action debit.
observations.action: Tested the reachable neighbours instead: two real trait-reduced debits (50 -> 25 and 25 -> 12), a real promise with zero room (Consumed [1], Applied [], 99 energy) and two concurrent refunds sharing one budget ([5] then nothing, 99 energy). Recorded here so the gap is not silent.
observations.confidence: high for the reachability argument; the untested state remains untested

observations.happened: The Cut253 gate native runtime key d445c9825416e54e is not reproducible from any current fast-profile core rlib (all four candidates give different keys).
observations.cause: The Cut257 production commit 43aa5655 changed ai.rs, class_advanced.rs and class_tree.rs after that gate closed; the audit's recorded inputs differ in exactly those three files.
observations.action: Recorded both epochs in production-identity-before/after-tests.json. This cfg(test)-only phase's binding contract is byte-identity of every production input, rlib candidate, native binary and WASM across its own edits, which holds.

limits: Controlled arenas, masks, RNG-selected branches and hand-set clocks/clocks leftovers are component fixtures, not earned public campaigns or claims about how often a branch fires in play.
Only priority item 4's seven sub-items are covered; the other matrix dimensions (armed-charge refusals, routing, hazards) stay with priority 1-3 and their own limits.
No pacing/full gate, no wasm or release build, no client test and no fun/balance claim was made or inferred; the production identity files pin the bytes those prior proofs stand on.
